shortName: University of Central Florida College of Medicine

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Office of Acceptance, Belonging, & Community Engagement is charged with advancing the University of Central Florida College of Medicine’s recruiting and retention of excellent students, faculty, and staff to address best the healthcare needs of our local community and nation. It also delivers education and supports scholarships that empower physicians and researchers to eliminate health disparities while engaging in impactful outreach throughout our Central Florida Communities. Lastly, it seeks to nurture a community of belonging for all our students, faculty, and staff.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students who are unable to continue enrollment or complete required instructional modules or clerkships due to illness, maternity leave of absence, hardship or special circumstances may request a leave of absence. A student in good academic standing without deficiencies may request of the Associate Dean for Students a leave of absence for a fixed period of time to conduct research or other scholarly activity. A student in good academic standing without deficiencies may request of the Associate Dean for Students a leave of absence for a fixed period of time as a result of a health problem or other personal circumstances that prevent concentration on academics. The Associate Dean for Students may approve a leave of absence for up to one calendar year.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Our growing body of 480 students has established more than 60 student-oriented organizations ranging from student government and medical-related student interest groups to local and global medical service groups.  They have already made a strong impact with their record of participation in community health events, intramural sports, and other related activities.  Visit our website for more information https://med.ucf.edu/student-affairs/student-services/student-organizations/.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The M.D. program occupies a state-of-the-art Medical Education Building in Lake Nona Medical City.  The Medical Education Building incorporates the latest educational technology to support the lecture halls, small group rooms, health sciences library, anatomy lab, team learning lab, clinical skills center, and simulation laboratories.  The UCF Health Sciences Campus at Lake Nona is located at the center of the Medical City that currently includes the UCF Lake Nona Medical Center, the UCF Cancer Research Center, the Orlando VA Medical Center, the National SimLEARN Center, the Nemours Children's Health, HCA and the University of Florida Research Center, among others.  In addition, medical City is adjacent to the Lake Nona Sports and Performance District, home to U.S. Tennis.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: On-campus housing is not available. However, a comprehensive list of medical student housing in the Lake Nona Medical City area is available.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
- The COM "LGBTQ+ Medical Student Allies" organization actively supports all students.  
- Many COM staff and faculty members are trained and identified as Safe Zone members.  These qualified individuals are known to LGBTQ+ students as a safe place to go for support. 
- The COM Counseling and Wellness Office at the COM is also available to all medical students who need to privately discuss any anxiety, stress, or other life concerns.  This office has also trained several upper-class men to assist other medical students in coping with the stressors and anxieties of medical school.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Counseling is available for medical students through Counseling & Wellness Services at the Health Sciences Campus at Lake Nona. Although CWS is separate from main campus Counseling & Psychological Services, as enrolled UCF students, you may use main campus services, including their after-hours crisis hotline. 

At CWS, counseling services are free to all currently enrolled students. Services are also confidential (except for a few specific legal exceptions), and counseling records are separate from academic records. Below is a list of specific services available at CWS to enrolled UCF medical students:

Individual therapy
Referrals to UCF psychiatrists
Group psychotherapy
Workshops and outreach related to wellness and mental health
Couple’s therapy (one partner needs to be an enrolled student)
Crisis intervention services
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: The culture of the University of Central Florida's (UCF) M.D. program centers around a strong commitment to innovation, collaboration, and community engagement. UCF fosters a supportive and collaborative environment where students are encouraged to work across disciplines and embrace a patient-centered approach to medicine. The program emphasizes hands-on learning, with early clinical experiences promoting real-world knowledge application. UCF ensures that students are well-prepared clinically and equipped to address the unique health needs of varying populations. With a forward-thinking curriculum, state-of-the-art facilities, and a close-knit faculty-student relationship, the culture of UCF's M.D. program cultivates future physicians who are both compassionate and adaptable, ready to lead in an evolving healthcare landscape.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Generally comfortable and casual dress is required except for clinical skills or patient training interactions.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Student Academic Support Services offers many resources. Students may participate in a free Peer Coaching Program to hone study/test-taking skills in 1x1, small/large groups with peer coaches.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Immediately in the Clinical Skills Center to learn H&P skills. Work with patients in a live clinical environment beginning in the first year curriculum and throughout their remaining years.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Instruction is applied through various active learning methods, including case-based learning, lecture, lab, simulation, web-based, team-based, project-based, and clinical preceptorships.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Rotations include Surgery, Internal/Family Med, OB/Gyn, Psychiatry, Neurology, and Pediatrics during the third year at major teaching hospitals throughout Florida.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: No, other than what is required for the Medical Student Performance Evaluation (Dean's Letter) that is produced for the Residency Application.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance is required where teamwork is needed to meet the goal of the lecture.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The UCF M.D. program curriculum integrates basic and clinical sciences across all four years. The first two years of the curriculum are structured into systems-based modules designed around clinical cases to integrate the various basic science disciplines and health systems science with a clinical practice focused on providing a deep understanding of normal and abnormal pathophysiology.   The curriculum also integrates psychosocial issues, cultural differences, communication skills, and physical diagnosis skills as they relate to the different topics in medicine.

The final two years are devoted to the core clinical sciences phase (clinical clerkships) and the individualization phase  (electives), complemented by didactics and small-group case application exercises. In addition, both years include a Capstone week focused on preparation for board examinations and the transition to residency.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Early Clinical Experiences: The practice of medicine is integrated within the first two years of the curriculum to prepare students for the clinical aspects of medicine. Specific areas of instruction include interpersonal communication skills, physical examination, and medical documentation skills. The first two years include the Community of Practice. This longitudinal experience provides a structured interaction with the Central Florida medical community, emphasizing the application of newly acquired clinical skills. Students are assigned to preceptors in primary care specialties to get early exposure to these areas. In addition, students develop a mentor-mentee relationship with their preceptors by working together in the first and second years to receive ongoing support and feedback on developing clinical skills.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: All students will participate in the Focused Individualized Research Experience (FIRE) project, which spans the first two years of the curriculum. Students will receive training, tools, and mentorship to successfully conduct a rigorous, independent, scholarly research project. Students will demonstrate and improve analytic, creative, and critical-thinking skills. The project may be in any area of interest related to medicine, including basic biomedical research, clinical research, public and community health, medical education, health administration and policy, biomedical engineering, ethics, and humanities. Research projects will culminate in oral/poster presentations at the FIRE Conference.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Most of the students recognize that this will help them in their application for a top residency.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Information about the Focused Individualized Research Experience (FIRE) program may be found at this link https://med.ucf.edu/research/m-d-student-research/fire/.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: UCF Lake Nona, HCA Osceola, HCA Oviedo, HCA Lake Monroe, HCA Ocala, HCA North Florida, Orlando VA Medical Center, Nemours Children's Hospital, Bay Pines VA, Flagler Hospital, NCH Healthcare System
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: A hybrid system that includes Honors/High Pass/Pass/Fail.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: UCF's vision is to have the nation's premier 21st-century college of medicine. Fully integrated into the Central Florida community's healthcare and medical research infrastructure, clinical training may occur within several hospitals associated with HCA, VA, Nemours Children's Hospital, and others across Florida. Our hospital partners provide students diverse clinical opportunities at over 13 major facilities. UCF's Biomedical Sciences faculty conducts groundbreaking research in cancer, cardiovascular, neurological, and infectious diseases, capitalizing on UCF's strengths in biomedical sciences, modeling, simulation, optics, and photonics. The Central Florida community has embraced UCF COM's future physicians, with more than 2,300 local healthcare professionals contributing as volunteer faculty. The UCF Lake Nona Hospital & UCF Cancer Center are also part of our Health Sciences campus. The UCF College of Nursing recently opened a facility adjacent to the MD Program.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The University of Central Florida College of Medicine educates and inspires individuals to be exemplary physicians and scientists, leaders in medicine, scholars in discovery, and adopters of innovative technology to improve the health and well-being of all.
Our patient-centered mission is achieved by outstanding medical care and services, groundbreaking research, and leading-edge medical and biomedical education in a diverse environment.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Please refer to our website for additional information: https://med.ucf.edu/admissions.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Applicants are required to submit at least three letters of recommendation. We need at least one of your letters from a former science professor who can adequately speak to your academic readiness and personal suitability for pursuing and practicing medicine.
Non-traditional applicants may submit a letter from a supervisor instead of the required faculty letter. 
Professors, advisors, research coordinators or preceptors, supervisors, coaches, mentors, and personal and professional colleagues may write additional letters. 
Pre-Health Advising Committee letter/packet may fulfill our letter requirements. 
All letters must be provided via AMCAS in a single packet, individually, or as a mixture. Letters must include the author's signature and contact information and should ideally be on letterhead. We will not consider applications for an interview until we receive all required letters. Ideally, letters will be <1 year old upon submission.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Once a student has participated in two Zoom-based interviews, they attend a mandatory three-hour virtual visit. 

The virtual visit will include:
•	Q&A with the COM Leadership
•	Overview of the curriculum
•	A student panel
•	Overview of the admissions committee decision process, timelines, and future communication and assistance

Opportunities to tour the facilities will be available throughout the admission cycle. Dates will be provided when students are invited to interview.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two, partially closed, virtual interviews.  Interviewers will not have access to academic institutions, grades, MCAT scores or letters . Interviewees will receive instructions prior to their interview date.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews will be conducted via Zoom.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: If still considered a dependent of a FL resident an applicant may be able to reclassify their residency for tuition purposes. Necessary documentation and approval required.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Up to 35% of each class is accepted from out-of-state.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Applicant must be a U.S. Citizen. Degrees accepted from some Canadian institutions and will be at the discretion of the Office of Admissions.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The UCF College of Medicine Admissions Office will abide by the recommendations of the Application and Acceptance Protocols for Admissions Officers outlined on the AAMC website.  Letters of Intent to enroll will be accepted and should be sent only by students who fully intend to enroll in the UCF MD program, should an offer of admission be made.  UCF COM Admissions Office will not make an offer to a student who has been reported as matriculated to another MD institution.

The UCF MD Admissions Office upholds high standards of professionalism and transparency throughout the admissions process.  Applicants have consistently lauded the UCF Admissions Office for its transparency in communicating admissions processes and advice to applicants.  We believe the more an applicant knows, the better off we all are.  Your decision to enroll in an MD program is life-changing.  We are happy to assist our applicants in considering their offers, whether they intend to enroll in UCF or another program.  However, professionalism begins with the admissions process.  Any accepted student may be dismissed from the program for unprofessional conduct during the admissions cycle.  Please review and adhere to the AAMC Protocols for Applicants.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: MCAT scores are considered among many other factors during the holistic review of an application. Additional factors include rigorous academic performance, demonstrated medical motivation through medical volunteering and shadowing, community service, teamwork and leadership activities, and research. While research is not required, it may strengthen an application.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: A minimum MCAT of 500 taken in the last three years (2023, 2024, and 2025) is required to be considered for an interview.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: A minimum 3.0 BCPM and 3.0 overall GPA is required to be considered for an interview.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Suppose an applicant did not meet the minimum 3.0 BCPM and overall GPA required through their undergraduate coursework. In that case, they may still be considered if they earn at least 20 core science credits through postbac or graduate coursework with a 3.0 or higher BCPM and overall GPA.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: If an applicant did not meet the minimum 3.0 BCPM and overall GPA required through their undergraduate coursework they may still be considered if they earn at least 20 core science credits through postbac or graduate coursework with a 3.0 or higher BCPM and overall GPA.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: The UCF College of Medicine has no policy prohibiting applicants from taking courses online or at a community college.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: UCF allows up to three updates to be uploaded through an applicant's portal.  Updates should be limited to significant activities not provided initially on the AMCAS or secondary applications.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: While financial status is not a consideration for admission to UCF, the Office of Student Financial Services works closely with medical students to keep their loan debt to a minimum. To date, every medical student who has attended UCF has been offered gift aid to help reduce the cost of attendance. Student Financial Services staff also guides budgeting and money management during personal counseling sessions and presentations year-round.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Applicants accepted between October 16th and April 30th will be given two weeks to respond to admissions offers via their portal.  There will be no deposit required to hold a seat.
Per AAMC Protocol, Applicants are required to reduce their accepted offers to no more than three acceptance offers by April 15 and one offer by April 30.
Applicants accepted between May 1st and June 30th will be allowed five business days to accept or decline admissions offers via their portal. No deposit will be required to hold a seat.

Use of Plan to Enroll (PTE) will be available to applicants on Feb 19.  Use of PTE is voluntary until May 1. Starting May 1, accepted students holding a seat at UCF COM will be required to select PTE through the AMCAS CYMS portal.
Accepted applicants must complete the Commit to Enroll process by June 15th. Please visit our website for more information regarding UCF COM policies on Choose Your Medical School tools.
Applicants accepted between July 1 and August 3 will be allowed two business days to accept or decline admission offers via their portal. No deposit will be required to hold a seat.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Students waitlisted will know their position and probability of being accepted.  Applicants will receive updates every 4-6 weeks for the duration of their time on this list beginning in late November.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: Prerequisite courses should be taken from a regionally accredited college or university in the United States.  Applicants must have completed at least a bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited college or university in the United States before enrollment into the M.D.  Program.  The UCF College of Medicine has no policy prohibiting applicants from taking courses online or at a community college.  Academic performance is one of many factors considered through the holistic review of an application.  Wherever possible, a student should choose the most rigorous possible academic preparation.  Biochemistry and Lab may be substituted for Organic II and Lab.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We recommend coursework to demonstrate competency in the area of prerequisite courses be completed within the last five years prior to submission of the AMCAS application.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Courses must be taken from a regionally accredited college or university in the United States.  The applicant meets the minimum GPA/MCAT requirements, and supplemental applications are provided to all qualified U.S. citizens and INS Permanent Residents with permanent Green Cards in their possession upon receipt of a verified AMCAS application.  Applications chosen for an interview will demonstrate high motivation, capability, passion, academic rigor, diverse skills, talents, and life experiences that will benefit the program, community, and classmates.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Consistent physician shadowing demonstrates medical motivation and an awareness of the profession's rigors. Therefore, physician scribing will often be included in this category for application evaluation.
